question: Express $$A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$ as the sum of a symmetric matrix and a skew-symmetric matrix.
explanation:
Decomposition of a square matrix
A square matrix can be written as $$A=\frac{1}{2}(A+A^T)+\frac{1}{2}(A-A^T)$$
Transpose
$$A^T=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1 \\ 5 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
Symmetric part
$$\frac{1}{2}(A+A^T)=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 \\ 4 & 4\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
Skew-symmetric part
$$\frac{1}{2}(A-A^T)=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 6 \\ -6 & 0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
Required representation
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
